_comment: Fragment 37 — D-84, the lane map corrected; orchestration is Lane A; G63 closed on scoping. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-84 — Orchestration Is Lane A, Not Lane C
nodes.description: D-75 assigned scripts/, .gitattributes and CI to Lane C as one undifferentiated build-tooling surface. Those files are orchestration, and orchestration is Lane A. Lane A writes every dependency before Lane C builds a workflow against it: CI calls bun run check, and Lane A writes what it calls. Lane C owns .github/workflows/ and nothing else.
nodes.rationale: Nothing is shared any more. The previous shared list existed only because the old map left build config unattributed; every path now maps to one lane or is reported as unmapped.

nodes.label: Two Cited Crossings Were Not Crossings
nodes.description: Re-probing forty commits under the corrected map, 24b39fb and 0e3705c touched only Lane A surfaces. D-75 and D-82 both cite 24b39fb as the unauthorized crossing on the grounds that it wrote scripts/checks/docs-drift.mjs and committed .gitattributes. Both files were that agent's own surface.
nodes.rationale: That commit's real defect is unchanged and unrelated: it recorded Q10 with a characterization contradicting the frozen Charter, which D-79 corrected. A scope error and a lane crossing were conflated. The three genuine multi-lane commits all predate D-75 and cannot have violated a rule that did not exist.

nodes.label: Lane A Can Build Every File-Based Control After All
nodes.description: Under the corrected map scripts/checks is Lane A, a pre-commit hook is orchestration and therefore Lane A, and .github/CODEOWNERS is Lane A because Lane C owns only workflows. What remains outside is branch protection, a GitHub setting rather than a file, belonging to no lane.
nodes.rationale: D-82's structural finding that nothing currently enforces the lanes stands unchanged. Only its claim about who could ever fix that was wrong, and D-83's sanctioned-crossing framing is withdrawn with it: building lane-boundary.mjs was never a crossing.

nodes.label: G63 — Union Is Right for Records and Wrong for Values
nodes.description: Tested on the rollback lineage: tag-01 fixed, tag-02 deployed, tag-01 merged into tag-02. Both sides' journal records survived, which is the Chief Editor's argument and it holds. On current-value content it fails: a status row merged to both Decided and Rejected, a version header appeared twice, and a union-duplicated CLAUDE.md sliced identically to a clean one so shared-core-hash passed on a file holding two full copies of the rules.
nodes.rationale: The file is the wrong unit: Modular_PRD.md and the register each carry append-only and current-value content together. Closed by scoping rather than removal, with docs/v1, Modular_PRD, the rule files and .agents set to merge=text. Union preserves text; the commit graph preserves audit.
